question: Should OpenClaw adopt tools.exec.denylist as the permanent config-owned STOP-list whose matches override full/off, allowlists, and durable trust across gateway, node, and macOS companion execution?
rationale: This introduces a new security/config contract and changes the meaning of otherwise permissive exec policy; tests can verify implementation, but they cannot choose the permanent operator and break-glass semantics.

options.title: Adopt the config-owned STOP list
options.body: Accept tools.exec.denylist as the sole persisted owner, require the documentation fix and integrated exact-head companion proof, then land the rebased branch.

options.title: Narrow the precedence contract
options.body: Require a revised design that preserves an explicit break-glass bypass or limits which permissive modes the denylist may override.

options.title: Decline the new policy surface
options.body: Keep the existing deny/allowlist/full model and close both implementation PRs and the feature request as not planned.

recommendation.title: Adopt the config-owned STOP list
recommendation.body: Accept tools.exec.denylist as the sole persisted owner, require the documentation fix and integrated exact-head companion proof, then land the rebased branch.

likelyOwner.reason: The history connects this person to the shipped exec-policy contract and repository security-boundary decisions.
